# REGIME READ — 2026-09-23

## Changes Since Previous Read
- **Stage: 2 → 2 (unchanged).** This is the second read in Stage 2. VIX is at 14.36 (2026-09-23, yfinance). That is still below the Stage-3 floor of 15 and inside Stage 2's band of 12–18. Stage 1 is still not available because we have no fresh evidence that breadth is strong.
- **Total score: −3 → −2 (delta +1).** One lens moved: **Cross-asset went from 0 to +1.** **That is the first bullish lens in ten reads.** The mix is now 1 bullish, 2 bearish and 4 neutral.
- **Triggers from previous read:**
  - *Bullish — NDX ≥ 30,000 with VXN below 19:* **HALF-FIRED, and still ARMED overall.** The price leg is well past the line: NDX is at 30,732.40, which is −0.1% from its 52-week high (snapshot). **The volatility leg went the wrong way.** VXN is at 20.18 (2026-09-22, engine), up from 19.29, so it would now need to fall 5.85%. The Nasdaq set a record ([Seoul Economic Daily](https://en.sedaily.com/international/2026/09/23/us-stocks-mixed-as-us-iran-talks-resume-brent-falls-below)) while Nasdaq volatility went up.
  - *Bullish — breadth above 45% of stocks over their 50-day average:* **ARMED, and there is no fresh reading.** The last broad-universe figure is 31.4% (2026-09-18, [thetrading.tools](https://www.thetrading.tools/market-breadth)).
  - *Bullish — a concluded US–China tariff-reduction announcement:* **ARMED, and still ahead of us.** Xi is now in Washington. The summit is Thursday 2026-09-24, and the truce expires in November ([Eastern Herald](https://easternherald.com/2026/09/21/xi-jinping-trump-summit-washington-trade-taiwan/), [Seoul Economic Daily](https://en.sedaily.com/international/2026/09/21/trump-xi-to-meet-at-white-house-on-the-24th-with-tech-ceos)).
  - *Bullish — Brent confirmed below $92:* **ARMED.** Brent is at $96.16 on the engine and $98.47 on the web (2026-09-22, [TradingEconomics](https://tradingeconomics.com/commodity/brent-crude-oil)). It needs to fall another 4.3% on the engine figure, or 6.6% on the web figure.
  - *Bearish — VIX back above 15:* **DID NOT FIRE.** VIX is at 14.36 and would need to rise 4.46%.
  - *Bearish — VXN > 22:* **DID NOT FIRE, but it moved closer.** VXN is at 20.18 and would need to rise 9.02% (it needed +14.0% last read).
  - *Bearish — NDX < 28,400:* **DID NOT FIRE, and moved further away.** NDX would need to fall 7.59%.
  - *Bearish — 10Y closing above 5.00% on two consecutive sessions:* **DID NOT FIRE.** The previous read's argument over one basis point on 09-18 **no longer matters.** The two latest closes are clearly below 5%:
    - 2026-09-21: 4.963% (engine).
    - 2026-09-22: 4.93%–4.951% ([CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/09/22/treasury-yield-us-bond-market-trump.html)).
  - *Bearish — HY OAS through 3.25% with IG above 0.90%:* **DID NOT FIRE, and moved away.** HY is at 2.66% (−4bp) and IG at 0.77% (−1bp), both 2026-09-21 (FRED). HY would need to widen by 59bp.
  - *Bearish — TQQQ below the 4-week low of $66.55:* **DID NOT FIRE.** Spot is 21.46% above it.
- **Notable lens flips:** Only one. **Cross-asset: 0 → +1.** Brent is below $100 on a checked print for the first time since 09-08, gold has no crisis bid and credit is tight. Dealer flow is the next closest to an upgrade, but it stays at 0 because VXN is rising alongside price.

## Regime Stage Tracker
- Current Stage: 2 — Mild bullish / grind
- Stage Anchor: 2026-09-18, the quad-witching close that finished the post-FOMC volatility crush. The underlying cause was the 2026-09-16 FOMC hike (25bp to 3.75%–4.00%, 12–0 vote).
- Position: Week 1 of an estimated 2–4. This is the second read in Stage 2.
- Confidence: Medium. Four lenses are neutral, one is bullish and two are bearish. That is not 5+ aligned. Breadth has still not confirmed the rally with fresh data.
- Bullish trigger (-> next bullish stage): any one of these:
  - Broad-universe breadth above 45% of stocks over their 50-day average (last reading 31.4%).
  - VXN below 19 (−5.85%) while NDX holds above 30,000.
  - A concluded truce extension or tariff reduction at the 09-24 summit.
- Bearish trigger (-> next bullish stage's opposite, Stage 3): any one of these:
  - VIX above 15 (+4.46%).
  - VXN above 22 (+9.02%).
  - NDX back below 30,000 (−2.38%) on a close, or below 28,400 (−7.59%).
  - The 10Y closing above 5.00% on two consecutive sessions (+0.74% from 4.963%).
  - HY OAS through 3.25% with IG above 0.90%.

## Regime Verdict
The Nasdaq is at record highs with VIX at a series low, credit tightening and oil falling on direct US–Iran talks, but the rally is still narrow and Nasdaq volatility is rising alongside price. Medium confidence.

**Data note:** WebSearch was available, so this is a full read with no confidence cap. Five items need care:
1. **The snapshot's "As of" labels mix dates.**
   - The Nasdaq Composite level of 27,244.28 is the **09-22** close, not 09-21 ([TheStreet](https://www.thestreet.com/stock-market-today/stock-market-today-dow-jones-sp-500-nasdaq-updates-sept-22-2026), [Seoul Economic Daily](https://en.sedaily.com/international/2026/09/23/us-stocks-mixed-as-us-iran-talks-resume-brent-falls-below)). That session's move was +0.45%, not +2.26%.
   - The DJI level of 52,048.83 is the 09-21 close. The 09-22 close was 51,863.69.
   - I copied the table verbatim as instructed. The Day Change column appears to span more than one session.
2. **The Brent feed still reads low, but the gap has narrowed.** The engine shows $96.16. The web shows $98.47 for 09-22 ([TradingEconomics](https://tradingeconomics.com/commodity/brent-crude-oil)) and "~$98–99" ([Seoul Economic Daily](https://en.sedaily.com/international/2026/09/23/us-stocks-mixed-as-us-iran-talks-resume-brent-falls-below)). That is about a $2.3 gap, down from about $4.7. This is the fourth straight read where the engine is low. Tickerdaily's "$89.62" is WTI.
3. **The TQQQ 09-22 close of $80.83 is the live-chain spot** (2026-09-22T20:45Z). I could not confirm it from an independent source. The $78.91 close for 09-21 is corroborated.
4. **RSI(14) for 09-22 was not computed.** The 64.0 figure is from 09-21.
5. **The news daemon now reads CLEAR / 0.0.** That broadly agrees with my read (score 3, all headlines de-escalatory). Last read's false 10.0 has not recurred.

Not retrieved: AAII, CFTC COT, NAAIM (behind a paywall since 2026-08-01), margin debt, ETF flows, Citi Economic Surprise, insiders and buybacks, Copper/Gold, transports, Bitcoin, and fresh broad-universe breadth.

## Diverging Signals
- **Price vs participation.** The Nasdaq Composite is at a record, but the Russell 2000 is 6.3% below its high. The last broad-universe breadth reading had 31% of stocks above their 50-day average. A few large companies are still carrying the index.
- **Price vs Nasdaq volatility.** NDX made a record and VXN rose 4.6% (19.29 → 20.18), while VIX fell to 14.36. The Nasdaq-specific volatility gauge is moving away from the broad one. For a TQQQ put seller, VXN is the gauge that matters, and it is going the wrong way for calm.
- **Rates vs dollar.** The 10Y fell back below 5% and credit tightened, but DXY rose 0.44%. The dollar has not confirmed that rate pressure is easing.
- **Headlines vs outcomes.** Geopolitics improved on process (US–Iran talks, Xi's arrival), but nothing has been concluded. The summit is a binary event on 09-24.

## TQQQ Read
- **Momentum: neutral, but getting hot.** RSI(14) was 64.0 on 09-21, up from 52.1, and the fund added another +2.43% on 09-22. TQQQ has had five green days in a row and is up 11.27% over the last two sessions ($72.64 → $80.83). RSI is only about 6 points from the 70 overbought line (where a move is considered stretched). For a put seller, the mean-reversion help that comes after a sell-off is gone. The risk now is a pullback after a stretched run, not a continued slide.
- **Market structure: SIDEWAYS.**
  - RALLY fails: spot is 21.46% above the 4-week low of $66.55, but it needs more than 30% (that line is $86.52).
  - DOWNTURN fails on both legs: spot is at the 4-week high, not 20% below it, and VXN is 20.18, below 25.
  - This is the eighteenth consecutive SIDEWAYS read. The RALLY line is now only 7.0% away.
- **Trend: uptrend on both horizons.**
  - Spot is 14.41% above the 50DMA. The reclaim has now held four sessions.
  - Spot is about 29.6% above the 200DMA.
  - Even the bottom of the expected-move band ($73.94) sits above the previous read's 4-week high.
- **Volatility & premium environment: the seller's cushion shrank for a second read in a row.**
  - IV/HV (20d) fell from 1.29 to **1.18**. Options now cost only about 18% more than the fund has actually been moving.
  - Realized volatility jumped from 39.4% to **48.1%**. The +8.63% day on 09-21 was itself a large move.
  - The quoted ATM IV is 57%, up from 51%. It is rising with VXN, but more slowly than realized volatility.
  - Premium is higher in dollar terms, but it is barely above fair value for how the fund actually moves.
- **Put-selling context: CAUTIOUS.**
  - **Leg (i) of the three-leg test is no longer in doubt.** Two clean consecutive 10Y closes below 5.00% (09-21 at 4.963%, 09-22 at 4.93%–4.951%) settle last read's one-basis-point question in favour of CAUTIOUS.
  - **Legs (ii) and (iii) also pass:** VXN is 20.18, below 25, and spot is 21.46% above the 4-week low.
  - **FAVOURABLE still misses one of its three legs.**
    - Brent below $100 on a checked print: **now MET** ($98.47, 09-22).
    - The 50DMA reclaim holding: **MET.**
    - VXN below 19: **FAILED and moved away.** It is 20.18 and would need to fall 5.85%.
  - **What argues for caution beyond the label:**
    - The fund has run 11% in two sessions straight into a binary summit on 09-24.
    - The seller's cushion (IV/HV 1.18) is the thinnest of this series.
    - Realized volatility is 48%.
    - Breadth has not been refreshed and was last at 31%.
  - **HOSTILE would return on any one of these:**
    - The 10Y at or above 5.00% on two consecutive closes.
    - A close below $66.55.
    - VXN above 25 (+23.9%).
    - HY above 3.25% with IG above 0.90%.

  This is context only — no strikes, expiries, sizes, or trade calls.

## Forward Levels & Triggers
- Bullish trigger: VXN below 19 while NDX holds 30,000 (this would also move the put-selling label to FAVOURABLE). Other routes: TQQQ closing above $86.52, which flips the structure to RALLY; or broad breadth above 45%.
- Bearish trigger: NDX closing back below 30,000 (−2.38%); VXN above 22 (+9.02%); VIX above 15 (+4.46%); or TQQQ back below the $79.49 prior 4-week high and then the $70.65 50DMA (−12.59%).
- Neutralizer: The Trump–Xi summit on 2026-09-24. A truce extension removes the November expiry risk. A breakdown puts the tariff channel back in play with the Nasdaq sitting at a record.

- 2026-09-24: Trump–Xi White House summit on the truce extension, rare earths and AI, with tech CEOs attending ([Seoul Economic Daily](https://en.sedaily.com/international/2026/09/21/trump-xi-to-meet-at-white-house-on-the-24th-with-tech-ceos)).
- Ongoing: follow-up rounds of US–Iran talks. Dates are not announced ([Seoul Economic Daily](https://en.sedaily.com/international/2026/09/23/us-iran-hold-three-hour-talks-at-un-as-oil-falls-below-100)).
- 2026-09-30: quarter-end rebalance.

## Expiry-Window Flag

- Window: EVENT-WINDOW. No macro or central-bank release is scheduled in the window, but a head-of-state trade summit with a hard truce deadline is.

## Structural Calendar Flag (deterministic — always report)
- **Quad-witching:** next is 2026-12-18, 86 days away. It is not within 2 sessions.
- **Quarter-end rebalance:** 2026-09-30 (Wednesday), 5 sessions away. It is not within 2 sessions, but it enters that zone on 09-28. Funds may need to rebalance after an equity-heavy quarter-end run in the Nasdaq.
- Net: Neither is inside 2 sessions today. The quarter-end becomes relevant from Monday 09-28. Expect heavier closing-auction volume and possible drift then. This is descriptive only.

## EVENT ALERT — Historical Playbook
- **Trump–Xi summit, 2026-09-24:**
  - **Comparable episodes:** the Busan meeting of late October 2025 that produced the current truce, and the May 2026 Beijing meeting ([Eastern Herald](https://easternherald.com/2026/09/21/xi-jinping-trump-summit-washington-trade-taiwan/), [Rappler timeline](https://www.rappler.com/world/us-canada/timeline-trump-xi-tariff-war-trade-truce/)).
  - **What I could not retrieve:** reliable day-by-day SPX/NDX and VIX/VXN reactions around those two meetings. I will not estimate them.
  - **General shape of the 2025 episodes:** markets rose into announced trade de-escalation and sold off sharply on escalation. The April 2025 tariff shock was a capitulation event, and the pause that followed marked the turn to risk-on. That pattern is lopsided: escalation surprises have moved the Nasdaq far more than confirmations of an expected truce.
  - **Current expectations:** already tempered — an extension traded for rare-earth access, with AI principles going no further than broad statements ([cryptobriefing](https://cryptobriefing.com/trump-xi-white-house-trade-truce-talks/)).
- **Net alert:** TQQQ is going into the summit after a five-day, +11% two-session run, with rising VXN and a thin cushion (IV/HV 1.18). An extension is largely expected and may do little. A breakdown would hit a stretched, narrow rally with gap risk that current premium barely covers. The risk leans to the downside for short-put exposure carried through 09-24. This is descriptive only — no trade calls.
